# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 57 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 40-41 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_057_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 57

**1** Jesus said: "The kingdom of the Father is like a person who had good [nanoue] seed [sperma].

**2** His enemy [djadj] came by night and sowed weeds [zizania] among the good seed.

**3** The person did not let them pull up the weeds; he said to them, 'I am afraid that you will go to pull up the weeds and pull up the wheat [hte] along with them.'

**4** For on the day of the harvest the weeds will be plainly visible, and they will be pulled up and burned."

---

**Textual Notes (EMET):**
- nanoue: good
- sperma: seed; Greek loan-word
- djadj: enemy; the one who acts in opposition
- zizania: weeds/tares; Greek loan-word zizanion (darnel grass, which resembles wheat)
- hte: wheat
- cf. Matt 13:24-30 — the Parable of the Weeds (Tares) — very close parallel
- Thomas's version is shorter; lacks Matt's allegorical interpretation (13:36-43)
- Key difference: in Thomas, "the person did not let them pull up the weeds" — the master forbids intervention
- In Matthew, the servants ask and the master explains; in Thomas, the master simply acts to prevent premature weeding
